page.title: Journal – Adding Entries - TachoMobile 2
page.heading: Journal – Adding Entries
page.subtitle: Learn how to add manual entries and create activity sequences

sections.timeModel:
1. How entries and their time work

Each entry has a start time. An entry normally continues until the start of the next entry. The last entry continues until the current time.

When you insert a new entry between two existing entries, the previous entry is shortened so that it ends when the new entry starts. The next existing entry keeps its original start time. This is how the Journal timeline is constructed.

For example:

  • 10:00 – Driving
  • 11:00 – Work
  • 12:00 – Rest

If you add Other work at 10:30, the timeline becomes:

  • Driving: 10:00–10:30
  • Other work: 10:30–11:00
  • Work: 11:00–12:00

The new entry takes over the time from its start until the next existing entry, while the following entry still starts at the same time.
sections.addingMethods:
2. Ways to start adding an entry

A manual entry can be started in two ways.

Context menu

Open the context menu for an existing entry and select Add → Single Entry. The selected entry provides the context for the new entry. The application restricts the possible time so that the new entry cannot be placed before the selected entry or after the next existing entry.

Global + button

Use the global + button and select Single Entry. This method is not tied to a particular existing entry, so you can select any time. The difference is that context-menu adding is bounded by the selected and following entries, while global adding is independent of a specific entry.
sections.activityTypes:
3. Choosing the activity or event

The first step is selecting what should be added. The available options are grouped as follows.

Main activities

  • Driving
  • Work
  • Availability
  • Rest

Point events

  • Border crossing
  • Loading / unloading
  • Ferry / train

Tachograph events

  • Shift started
  • Shift ended
  • Card inserted
  • Card removed

Main activities build the primary activity timeline. Point events are special events that occur within a main activity and do not interrupt its continuity. Card inserted is also a special event and does not normally interrupt the main activity.

Shift started and Shift ended are different: they are treated as main activities, so they interrupt the previous main activity.

Card removed does not interrupt the current main activity. Instead, from the moment the card is removed, the application assumes that the driver is resting and changes the activity to Rest. This rest can then be interrupted by adding a manual activity.

For example, if Rest is running and you add Card inserted, Rest continues. If you add Shift started at that moment, Rest ends at that time and the new activity begins.

The main menu uses combined operations: starting work simulates both card insertion and shift start, while ending work simulates both shift end and card removal. When entered manually, these events still have different timeline semantics: Card inserted is a special event, Card removed changes the activity to Rest, while Shift started and Shift ended behave as main activities.
sections.singleEntry:
4. Adding a single manual entry

Step 1 – Select the activity/event

Select the activity or event that you want to add.

Step 2 – Edit entry details

Adjust the entry details in the same way as when entering an activity from the main menu:

  • Vehicle registration number
  • Country
  • City
  • Odometer
  • Date and time
  • Notes

For a single entry, finish the entry after editing these details.
sections.sequence:
5. Adding a sequence of entries

The Start Work / Stop Work options also let you create a sequence of activities without confirming every entry separately.

  1. Select the first activity.
  2. Edit its details and time.
  3. Select Next instead of finishing.
  4. Select the next activity.
  5. Specify its start time, or specify its start time and duration.
  6. When a duration is specified, the next activity can be positioned automatically after that duration, allowing you to build the sequence efficiently.
  7. Continue adding activities.
  8. Back cancels the last step of the sequence and returns to the previous step.
  9. Only Finish creates and applies the complete sequence to the Journal.

The entries are not actually created as a completed sequence until you select Finish.

For example, a sequence can be: Shift started → Work → Driving → Work → Rest.
sections.range:
6. Creating a complete simulated shift

The relevant Start Work / Stop Work functionality also provides a Range option. It is available both from the context menu and from the global + button. Range allows you to create a complete shift by defining its time range and activities.

Shift start

Choose whether the shift starts at a specific date and time or after a specified amount of rest time, for example after a daily rest period.

Depending on the selected option, enter either the start date and time or how much rest time has elapsed up to the current moment.

Shift duration

Choose between the following modes:

Activity total — the shift duration is built from the individual activities, including rest periods that are explicitly part of the shift.

Fixed shift duration — define the total duration of the shift and specify the duration of the individual activities. The remaining time is automatically filled with rest.

When the remaining time is filled with rest, the application places rest periods so that the required 45-minute break is maintained before 4.5 hours of driving is exceeded.

Additional shift information

You can also specify:

  • Vehicle registration number
  • Starting odometer
  • Ending odometer
  • Whether the applicable rules should account for international transport
  • Whether the trip is an occasional bus/coach transport operation

The generated shift preserves the correct timeline and calculates the resulting mileage from the starting and ending odometer values.
